title: Education What I Built Instead mrsk04
author: mrsk04
summary: A mother and teacher who writes under the pseudonym mrsk04 documents her experience navigating a school system that repeatedly reassured her that her dyslexic daughter was 'doing great' -- and the slow grief of discovering those assurances were wrong. Moving from South Pasadena's exemplary school district to Colorado, the author believed she had found an equivalently strong system and placed full trust in it, only to realize over time that the school's confidence about her daughter's progress had been masking an unaddressed reading gap. The article chronicles not just the practical failures -- inadequate assessment, missed red flags, delayed intervention -- but the emotional experience of a parent doing everything right while watching the system fail her child. The title refers to the alternative scaffolding the author ultimately built herself: tutoring, advocacy, her own dyslexia research, and this Substack as a resource for other parents in the same position.
points: The specific grief of watching a system fail your child while doing everything right -- trusting the professionals, attending every meeting, believing the assurances -- is a distinct emotional experience that many parents of children with learning differences carry silently.

School systems that give reassuring progress reports about struggling students are not necessarily lying; they are often operating within an assessment framework that cannot detect the specific deficit, particularly for twice-exceptional students whose strengths mask their gaps.

Dyslexia identification depends on specific screening tools many districts do not use routinely; without phonological awareness and decoding assessments, a bright, compensating child can pass all general assessments while falling further behind in actual reading skill.

When schools fail to identify a learning difference, the work of remediation falls to parents -- who must now become their own researchers, advocates, and often supplementary teachers on top of every other parental responsibility.

Because systems rarely self-correct based on individual parent complaints, public accountability and peer knowledge-sharing become the primary mechanisms for change in disability advocacy communities.
quotes: When we moved to the north Denver metro area, we were very intentional about where we purchased our home. Moving from South Pasadena, California was a difficult decision and one I frankly sometimes regret. South Pasadena schools have a reputation that is strongly backed with action.
